paper_title: Supersymmetric AdS solitons and the interconnection of different vacua of N = 4 Super Yang-Mills (Anabalon, 2024, JHEP)
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.}
For a regular soliton branch satisfying the period formula and Wilson-line definitions, eliminating \(q_1,q_2\) and \(\delta\) yields the source-only cubic constraint
\[
\psi_1^2x_0^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x_0^2
-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x_0+
\psi_2^4=0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad \delta>0,
\qquad k:=\frac{2\pi}{\delta}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta=2\pi\psi_1,
\qquad q_2(1-x_0)\delta=2\pi\psi_2.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\delta=\frac{2\pi x_0}{|A|}\sqrt{|B|},\\
& A:=2q_1^2-q_2^2x_0^2-q_2^2x_0,
\qquad B:=\frac{q_1^2-q_2^2x_0}{x_0-1}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{On the regular branch used below, } |B|=-B.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{All divisions below are by nonzero factors specified in (P1)--(P4).}
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First invert the source definitions:
\begin{align}
q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta&=2\pi\psi_1 &&\text{by (P2)}\\
q_1\frac{x_0-1}{x_0}&=k\psi_1 &&\text{by (P1)}\\
q_1&=\frac{k\psi_1x_0}{x_0-1}. \label{eq:q1-inv}
\end{align}
Similarly,
\begin{align}
q_2(1-x_0)\delta&=2\pi\psi_2 &&\text{by (P2)}\\
q_2(1-x_0)&=k\psi_2 &&\text{by (P1)}\\
q_2&=-\frac{k\psi_2}{x_0-1}. \label{eq:q2-inv}
\end{align}
Substitute \eqref{eq:q1-inv}--\eqref{eq:q2-inv} into \(A\) and \(B\):
\begin{align}
A
&=2q_1^2-q_2^2x_0^2-q_2^2x_0 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac{k^2}{(x_0-1)^2}\left(2\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2x_0\right) &&\text{substitution}\\
&=\frac{k^2x_0}{(x_0-1)^2}\left((2\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)x_0-\psi_2^2\right). \label{eq:A-sub}
\end{align}
Also,
\begin{align}
B
&=\frac{q_1^2-q_2^2x_0}{x_0-1} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac{k^2\psi_1^2x_0^2-k^2\psi_2^2x_0}{(x_0-1)^3} &&\text{substitution}\\
&=\frac{k^2x_0(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)}{(x_0-1)^3}. \label{eq:B-sub}
\end{align}
Now square the period formula:
\begin{align}
\delta&=\frac{2\pi x_0}{|A|}\sqrt{|B|} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
\frac{2\pi}{\delta}&=\frac{|A|}{x_0\sqrt{|B|}} &&\text{invert}\\
k^2&=\frac{A^2}{x_0^2|B|} &&\text{square and use (P1)}\\
0&=A^2-k^2x_0^2|B| &&\text{rearrange}\\
0&=A^2+k^2x_0^2B &&\text{use }|B|=-B\text{ from (P4)}. \label{eq:period-reduced}
\end{align}
Using \eqref{eq:A-sub} and \eqref{eq:B-sub}, the two terms in \eqref{eq:period-reduced} become
\begin{align}
A^2
&=\frac{k^4x_0^2}{(x_0-1)^4}\left((2\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)x_0-\psi_2^2\right)^2,\\
k^2x_0^2B
&=\frac{k^4x_0^3(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)}{(x_0-1)^3}\\
&=\frac{k^4x_0^2}{(x_0-1)^4}\left[x_0(x_0-1)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)\right].
\end{align}
Therefore \eqref{eq:period-reduced} is equivalent to
\begin{align}
0
&=\left((2\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)x_0-\psi_2^2\right)^2
+x_0(x_0-1)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2) &&\text{divide by }\frac{k^4x_0^2}{(x_0-1)^4}\\
&=(2\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)^2x_0^2
-2\psi_2^2(2\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)x_0
+\psi_2^4
+\psi_1^2x_0^3
-\psi_1^2x_0^2
-\psi_2^2x_0^2
+\psi_2^2x_0 &&\text{expand}\\
&=\psi_1^2x_0^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x_0^2\\
&\qquad -\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x_0+
\psi_2^4. &&\text{collect powers of }x_0
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\psi_1^2x_0^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x_0^2
-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x_0+
\psi_2^4=0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.}
The scalar fluctuation problem has three limiting spectral behaviours:
\[
z_0\neq0\Longrightarrow M=M_n\ \text{is discrete},
\qquad
(\epsilon,q_1,q_2)=(+1,0,0)\Longrightarrow M^2\ge\frac{\ell^2}{L^4},
\qquad
\ell=0,\ F(z)=1\Longrightarrow M^2\ge0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &-\frac{d^2\Psi}{du^2}+V(u)\Psi=M^2\Psi.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &z\to0\Longrightarrow u\to0,
\qquad V(u)\simeq\frac{15}{4u^2},\\
&\Psi(u)=\sqrt{Mu}\left[C_1J_2(Mu)+C_2Y_2(Mu)\right],
\qquad C_2=0\text{ at the UV endpoint}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &z_0\neq0\Longrightarrow u\to u_{\max}<\infty,
\qquad V(u)\simeq-\frac{1}{4(u-u_{\max})^2},\\
&\Psi(u)\simeq\sqrt{u_{\max}-u}\left[C_1'J_0(M(u-u_{\max}))+C_2'Y_0(M(u-u_{\max}))\right],
\qquad C_2'=0\text{ at the IR endpoint}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{A second-order Sturm--Liouville equation on }0<u<u_{\max}<\infty\text{ with one}\nonumber\\
&\text{homogeneous endpoint condition at each endpoint has eigenvalues given by isolated roots }H(M)=0.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &(\epsilon,q_1,q_2)=(+1,0,0)\Longrightarrow
z_0\text{ does not exist and }V(u)\to\frac{\ell^2}{L^4}\text{ as }u\to\infty.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{For }0<u<\infty\text{ with }V(u)\to V_\infty\text{ as }u\to\infty,
\text{ the continuum begins at }M^2=V_\infty.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\ell=0,
\qquad F(z)=1
\Longrightarrow u=z\in(0,\infty),
\qquad V(u)=\frac{15}{4u^2}.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &L>0,
\qquad \ell\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First suppose \(z_0\neq0\). Then the radial interval is finite:
\begin{align}
z_0\neq0
&\Longrightarrow 0<u<u_{\max}<\infty &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
The UV endpoint condition gives
\begin{align}
C_2&=0 &&\text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
The IR endpoint condition gives
\begin{align}
C_2'&=0 &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Therefore the allowed masses satisfy
\begin{align}
H(M)&=0 &&\text{by (P4)}\\
M&=M_n &&\text{isolated roots are indexed discretely}.
\end{align}
Next consider \((\epsilon,q_1,q_2)=(+1,0,0)\). Then
\begin{align}
V_\infty
&:=\lim_{u\to\infty}V(u) &&\text{definition}\\
&=\frac{\ell^2}{L^4} &&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Using the half-line spectral statement,
\begin{align}
M^2&\ge V_\infty &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\frac{\ell^2}{L^4}. &&\text{substitution}
\end{align}
Finally, for pure AdS,
\begin{align}
\ell=0,
\quad F(z)=1
&\Longrightarrow u=z\in(0,\infty),\quad V(u)=\frac{15}{4u^2} &&\text{by (P7)}\\
\lim_{u\to\infty}V(u)&=0 &&\text{take the limit}\\
M^2&\ge0 &&\text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{z_0\neq0\Longrightarrow M=M_n\ \text{is discrete},
\qquad
(\epsilon,q_1,q_2)=(+1,0,0)\Longrightarrow M^2\ge\frac{\ell^2}{L^4},
\qquad
\ell=0,\ F(z)=1\Longrightarrow M^2\ge0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
